en.content: Consider the following list of reagents, acidified K<sub>2</sub>Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub>, alkaline KMnO<sub>4</sub>, CuSO<sub>4</sub>, H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub>, Cl<sub>2</sub>, O<sub>3</sub>, FeCl<sub>3</sub>, HNO<sub>3</sub> and Na<sub>2</sub>S<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>. The total number of reagents that can oxidise aqueous iodide to iodine is
en.explanation:
Acidified K2Cr2O7, CuSO4, H2O2, Cl2, O3, FeCl3 and HNO3 oxidise aq. iodide to iodine. Alkaline KMnO4 oxidise aq. iodide to IO.

Na2S2O3 is a strong reducing agent which on reaction with I2 produces I.

Na2S2O3 + I2 2I + Na2S4O6

Therefore, no reaction takes place between Na2S2O3 and iodide ion. Hence, correct integer is (7).

en.content: Consider all possible isomeric ketones including stereoisomers of MW = 100. All these isomers are independently reacted with NaBH<sub>4</sub> (Note : stereoisomers are also reacted separately). The total number of ketones that give a racemic product(s) is/are
en.explanation: Molecular weight of the ketone is 100. So, molecular formula = C6H12O. The possible number of ketones with molecular formula C6H12O is six. Out of these, the total number of ketones that give a racemic product(s) on reaction with NaBH4 is 5. The structure with chiral carbon will not give racemic product on reduction.
